chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Qunut in the Witr prayer: Is there a specific supplication to be followed? It was said, and he said: 'Praise Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seek forgiveness for your great sin.' Then he said: 'Every sin is great.'

key_terms.اَلْقُنُوتُ: Supplication recited during prayer, specifically in the final rak'ah
key_terms.اَلْوَتْرُ: The odd-numbered night prayer, typically three rak'ahs
key_terms.مُوَقَّتٌ: Fixed or specific (referring to a set text)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed supplication for Qunut in the Witr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Qunut of Witr is not bound by a rigid, fixed text but allows for a flexible structure of praise, prophetic blessings, and repentance. By defining 'every sin' as 'great,' he emphasizes the comprehensive nature of human imperfection, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness with humility and sincerity rather than merely reciting a formula. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual essence of supplication over rigid formalism in optional prayers.
